task_name: The channel, wired and documented where this API is documented

rubric.result: The objective promises two things. (1) 'the running backend reaches all three endpoints': ct-api.ts now passes `liveSessions`, `new WatchLiveSession({ liveSessions })` and `new TypeIntoSession({ liveSessions })` to the ApiServer it already builds (ct-api.ts:472-474), which are exactly the collaborators `SessionStreamRoute.handledBy(this.liveSessions!, this.watchLiveSession!)` and `SessionInputRoute.handledBy(this.liveSessions!, this.typeIntoSession!)` consume in api-server.ts:254 and :262 and which were undefined until now. (2) 'they are in the contract the frontend codes against': API.md gains one section per endpoint in mounting order, the corrected count row, three rows in the 'Where the frontend consumes each one' table and the API_PATHS note; this-repository.md gains the Live session row; frontend/README.md gains the sessions paragraph. Both halves are produced by the diff.

The brief's TDD line reads 'No TDD — this task is documentation; its claims are measured by the predicates below and by the suites the earlier tasks left green.' The item has no assertion to compare, so it produces no finding.

Three blocks. Current state (backend/API.md) quotes '| Port | `CT_API_PORT`, default `8787` |', present verbatim at API.md:14. Final text (backend/API.md) '| Endpoints | 11 (`POST` 4, `GET` 7) |' is at API.md:17, and I counted the routes api-server.ts mounts: POST /start-plan, /implement-plan, /review-plan, /sessions/:id/input = 4; GET /plan-events, /active-plans, /implement-progress, /implement-history, /external-tools, /sessions, /sessions/:id/stream = 7; eleven, so the literal is the true number. Final text (backend/conventions/this-repository.md) appears verbatim at line 60, in alphabetical place between 'Harvest ledger' and 'Metrics delivery'. The prose contract of the task ('ct-api.ts passes liveSessions, new WatchLiveSession({ liveSessions }) and new TypeIntoSession({ liveSessions })') is matched name by name by the diff, with no extra collaborator and no renamed key.

Rows the diff bears on, checked one by one against the documented text. P-1 (synchronous port): the wiring passes the port itself so the route can find between headers — consistent. P-2 (a frame carries bytes and nothing else, no `kind` until slice #6): API.md:767-769 says exactly that. P-3 (the page never opens or kills a session; ct-api.ts opens one at start-up and owns it): API.md:734-735 and README's 'The backend owns the session, not the page ... opened once at the backend's start-up'; ct-api.ts:443 is the single open() in backend/src. P-5 (@xterm/xterm renders the stream): named in README. P-6 ($SHELL -il, /bin/sh fallback, name is the basename): API.md:736-741, matching PtyLiveSessions.LOGIN_INTERACTIVE, FALLBACK_SHELL and #basenameOf. P-7 (262144 characters, oldest dropped first, what a second subscriber gets first): API.md:769-777, matching SCROLLBACK_CHARACTERS and #trimmed. P-8 (English outside product copy): all three documents are English, no rendered copy touched. P-9 (session-not-live shared between the two vocabularies): API.md:785-787. D-10 (everything new under backend/ is TypeScript): the wired entrypoint is .ts. No row is reopened or implemented with a different value.

ct's yardstick, rule by rule on the five production lines of ct-api.ts and on the documents. conventions/defects.md, its four rules named: (a) closed vocabulary — no subject in this diff; it adds no value that classifies anything, and the vocabularies the documentation describes (SessionInputOutcome, SessionStreamOutcome) are frozen catalogues built in earlier tasks and dispatched through Projection with no catch-all. (b) raw map as the return value of logic — no subject; the object literal ct-api.ts hands ApiServer is a named-parameters argument at the composition root, the established idiom of that entrypoint, not a map returned by logic. (c) two fields that have to agree — no sentinel and no flag is added; I considered whether passing `liveSessions` beside the two use cases built over it is a pair that must agree, and it is not this diff's decision: that ApiServer signature and the `handledBy(liveSessions, useCase)` shape were fixed in tasks 1, 4 and 5, outside this task's Files, and this task writes the three lines its brief prescribes verbatim. (d) error named for where it happens — no subject; the diff declares no error. conventions/style.md: no prose added to code, English throughout, no free function (the additions are properties inside an existing static method). conventions/architecture.md: 'The outer edge of the program ... is the only place that assembles the dependency graph: it picks the concrete adapters and injects them' — ct-api.ts is that place and the injection is by name through the constructor, so the pattern of delivery here is the one the document prescribes. conventions/simplicity.md: each added field answers to a call that exists today — api-server.ts:254 and :262 would dereference undefined without them. conventions/decisions.md: the constants restated in API.md (262144, the endpoint count) are documentation of a contract, which is what backend/API.md exists for by the repo's own rule; backend/conventions/this-repository.md's new row adds a ubiquitous-language term and __tests__/conventions-no-restatement.test.ts, which guards that document, is green. Repo yardstick: AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md — all three documents are English and the Spanish exemption (what renders on the page) is untouched. I found no clash between a control of the plan and any of these documents.

No test file is touched. The `-` lines are in backend/API.md (the superseded '| Endpoints | 7 (`POST` 3, `GET` 4) |' row) and in the plan file; none of them removes, relaxes or rewrites an assertion, a case or a test. The amendment's edit to task 9's **Verification:** only adds commands (`npm --prefix backend run typecheck`, `npm --prefix backend test`) and rewords a comment, so nothing was made laxer there either.

The behaviour half of the objective is produced by production code: ct-api.ts:472-474 hands the routes their real collaborators over the real PtyLiveSessions built at ct-api.ts:439-443, and there is no double, stub or fixture anywhere in this diff. The rest of the task is documentation, judged as documentation: I checked every added claim against the code rather than against the implementer's report. The two repaired claims hold — PtyLiveSessions#exited deletes the session from #open (pty-live-sessions.ts:108-111) and `liveSessions.open()` occurs exactly once in backend/src (ct-api.ts:443), so 'nothing reopens it ... this answers {"sessions":[]} for the rest of the process's life' is now true in both documents; and SessionInputRequest.#isWellFormedText requires only `typeof given === 'string' && given.length > 0`, so 'not empty — a whitespace-only string still passes' is true. I also re-verified, and found true, every other added claim: the eleven-endpoint count against the routes api-server.ts mounts; 'sessions is always present' against SessionsRoute; the 202 body {"status":"typed","id":...} against session-input-route.ts:36; the four refusal rows against SessionInputRefusal's four projections and their details, including 'detail names the fields, sorted' against `unknown.sort()`; the stream's single frame kind against SessionStreamRoute.frameFor; 'the stream never ends on its own' against the route, which only ends the response on request 'close'; 'the first frame carries the scrollback, up to 262144 characters, oldest dropped first' against PtyLiveSessions.watch, SCROLLBACK_CHARACTERS and #trimmed; the second subscription replaying the scrollback against watch() returning `opened.scrollback`; 'session-not-live shared' against both routes' codes; 405/403 as the only shared refusals against api-server.ts's app.all and Browsers.turnAwayForeign's 403; the three frontend table rows against frontend/src/app/sessions/client.ts, which really does list, watch and type, and Sessions.types.ts; the API_PATHS prefix note against vite.config.ts:8, whose string key '/sessions' matches the two sub-paths as a prefix; and README's SessionsPanel/SessionTerminal/@xterm/xterm claims against SessionsPanel.tsx, SessionTerminal.tsx (Terminal from '@xterm/xterm', subscription.close() and terminal.dispose() on unmount) and Home.tsx:490-492, where SessionsPanel is rendered unconditionally. I found no third false claim.

Inside the four declared files every line traces to a sentence of the task: the three API.md sections in mounting order with their answers and refusals, the corrected count, the three frontend rows and the API_PATHS note, the single ubiquitous-language row, and the README paragraph naming the endpoints, @xterm/xterm and the backend's ownership. The eight existing endpoints named in **Out of scope** keep their paths, bodies, codes and answers — only the count row above them changed, which the task's own text asks for. ct-api.ts gains two imports and three properties and nothing else. The fifth path is the plan file, an amendment: it moves the ct-api.ts wiring from task 10 into task 9 (objective, **Files:**, Call site block turned into prose) and leaves task 10 as the end-to-end test alone. The task's own sentence justifies it — API.md's opening line, 'Every shape below was read from a running server', cannot be honoured for the stream and the input endpoint while nothing hands their routes their collaborators. I read the hunk line by line for disarmed controls and found the opposite: task 9's **Verification:** gains `npm --prefix backend run typecheck` and the full `npm --prefix backend test`, no test name or block declaration is dropped, and the only route removed from a **Files:** list is ct-api.ts from task 10, where it would now be a duplicate. The Current state (backend/API.md) block was re-pointed from the row this task replaces to the unchanged Port row above it; that is a weaker anchor but a coherent one, since the quoted row ceases to exist the moment this task edits it, and the load-bearing block (Final text) is present verbatim. Not worth a round trip.

The diff adds no test: its files are one entrypoint wiring and three documents, and no test file appears among the touched paths. There is no new test to measure for determinism, isolation or verification of real behaviour, so this item has no subject.
